candidate.answerReason: There are 9 choices for the thousands digit, followed by 9, 8, and 7 choices for the remaining distinct digits, giving 4536.

methods.label: Choose the digits from left to right
methods.explanation:
Choose each digit while excluding those already used. The thousands digit cannot be \(0\), so it has \(9\) choices. The hundreds digit can be any of the \(10\) digits except the thousands digit, giving \(9\) choices; \(0\) is now allowed. The tens digit then has \(8\) choices, and the ones digit has \(7\).

Multiplying these successive choice counts gives
\[
9\times9\times8\times7=4536.
\]
Every valid integer has exactly one sequence of these four digit choices, and every counted sequence gives a four-digit integer with distinct digits. The endpoints \(1000\) and \(9999\) repeat digits, so including or excluding them does not change the count.

The answer is \(\boxed{4536}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses four-digit place value and elementary successive-choice counting, without factorial notation.
